task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req178-dlq-routes.md or similar) for REQ-178: a new router/controller module exposing GET /api/v1/dlq (list, filterable independently by status/source_type-mapped-to-entry_type/search/instance_id, cursor-paginated via page_size/cursor, response {items: [DlqEntry], next_cursor}), GET /api/v1/dlq/:id (single DlqEntry), POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry (calls Letflow.Dlq.retry/2, returns updated DlqEntry), POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/discard (calls Letflow.Dlq.discard/2, returns updated DlqEntry). Design must specify: (1) the exact Plug/Router route definitions and how each maps its params to lib/letflow/dlq.ex's list/2 filter options; (2) the DlqEntry JSON serialization shape, matching web/src/types/api.ts field-for-field (id, entry_type, instance_id, reason, full_reason, retry_count, status, created_at at minimum); (3) the permission check mechanism -- every route requires DlqOperate from REQ-069's Letflow.Api.Authorization matrix, verify which roles actually hold it (do not assume PROCESS_OPERATOR/PLATFORM_ADMIN are correct without checking the real matrix) and specify the 403 response for a caller lacking it; (4) the cross-tenant-404 mechanism per REQ-072's INV-5 rule -- a real id belonging to another tenant must return 404, identical in shape to a genuinely nonexistent id, never 403; (5) the 409-shaped conflict response for retry/discard against an already-terminal (resolved/discarded) entry, distinct from a generic 500; (6) the moduledoc's explicit statement that R-Co's dlq.zig was not inspected (R-Co unreachable) and web/src/api/dlq.ts/web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead. Design only -- no implementation code, no fenced code block reproducing real .ex content (this project's mechanical, no-exceptions rule, caught real defects on REQ-157/174/176/177 in this exact pipeline).
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/dlq returns a body shaped exactly {items: [...], next_cursor: string|null}, and each item's field names (id, entry_type, instance_id, reason, full_reason, retry_count, status, created_at at minimum) match DlqEntry's, verified against web/src/types/api.ts rather than a hand-invented shape
GET /api/v1/dlq honors status, source_type, search, cursor and page_size independently, each with its own test demonstrating the filter narrows the result set

POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry and .../discard both require the DlqOperate permission from REQ-069's matrix -- a caller holding no role with that permission receives 403, and a caller from a different tenant naming a real id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403 -- three explicit tests

POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry and .../discard against a non-existent id return 404, and against an id already "resolved" or "discarded" return a 409-shaped conflict rather than a generic 500 -- covering the not-found and terminal-state cases each with their own test

the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's dlq.zig was not inspected in this batch (unreachable from the drafting environment) and that web/src/api/dlq.ts / web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead, so a future reader does not assume R-Co parity was verified when it wasn't
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
